headline: Sonny Gray paints a masterpiece as the Sox roll on
morning_brew: Sonny Gray was painting corners all night long against the White Sox, and watching him cruise through six frames made for a damn relaxing evening at the Fens. He matched a career high for wins, and frankly, he looked like the true ace we needed to keep this train moving down the tracks. I haven't seen a performance that surgical since cousin Jimmy once spent three hours trying to organize his basement before giving up and heading straight to the pub.

The bullpen finally did their part to lock down the victory, with Morán showing some nasty stuff to close out the ninth. We haven't seen the arson squad make an appearance in a while, and if these guys keep attacking the zone like this, I might actually stop watching the late innings through my fingers. It is a damn good feeling to see the pitching staff carry the load when the bats are taking a breather, and this group is starting to look like a legitimate contender for the post-season.

Looking ahead, we have a bunch of games at the yard before heading out to Toronto. The Patriots are still deep in the grind down in Foxborough, but for now, the focus is squarely on maintaining this momentum in the AL East. I am not gonna get ahead of myself and start booking hotels for October, but the vibe in the Hub is shifting, and for the first time in a while, it feels like we belong in the conversation.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox's Sonny Gray matches career high with AL-best 14th win
news_digest.dans_take: Seeing him sit at the top of the league in wins is the kind of stuff that makes me feel like a genius for believing in this rotation.
